137961.overview: Originality the power to produce something individual, is a prized gift. The creators of Logical offer you a unique concept as rare as their talents. The design is simple, the game fascinating and additive, the possibilities endless.

137962.overview: Loom is a 1990 fantasy-themed graphic adventure game by Lucasfilm Games. The project was led by Brian Moriarty, a former Infocom employee and author of classic text adventures Wishbringer (1985), Trinity (1986), and Beyond Zork (1987). It was the fourth game to use the SCUMM adventure game engine, and the first of those to avoid the verb–object interface introduced in Maniac Mansion.

164609.overview:
Your task is to rescue the Lemmings across 120 levels of fast-paced puzzling. These creatures simply walk blindly through the world in the hope of reaching safety at the end of the level - unfortunately these levels include steep drops, gaps in the ground, barriers and rivers amongst other hazards.

You are in control not of any individual Lemming, but of a cross-hair, which can be moved over any of the Lemmings. Along the bottom are a selection of functions which can be assigned to a Lemming, including climbing, floating and bashing. You must click to select the appropriate function, then click on the Lemming to activate it. Each level has a different range of skills on offer, a different amount of Lemmings, and a different percentage target in order to progress.

189802.overview:
LEARN FRENCH WITH Astérix. Learn French while you follow the exciting adventures of Asterix, the small but prodigiously brave warrior of Gaul, who draws his strength from a certain magic potion. In this story Asterix, more comfortable skirmishing with Romans than changing nappies, finds himself adopted by a very special baby. Find out how he copes! Whether you're fifteen or fifty... whether you're an enthusiastic beginner, or dusting down your old school French, or already strong in the language... whether you're studying on your own or taking classes... this program has something to offer.

Discs One and Two together give you:
• An entertaining story, with almost 60 minutes of spoken French in the words of over 30 different characters.
• Teaching notes for each caption, explaining vocabulary and grammatical points, and giving further related examples.
• Over 400 Uderzo cartoon drawings in full colour.
• A complete English translation of the story in text.
• Over 1500 vocabulary items.
